plain_english: The lord said: one who does duty as action without relying on its fruit is both renouncer and yogi, not one who merely abandons fire or action.
sanskrit_cite: atha ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ   śrībhagavānuvāca   anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ | sa saṃnyāsī ca  yogī ca na niragnirna cākriyaḥ

plain_english: What is called renunciation is yoga; know this, pandava. No one becomes a yogi without renounced resolve, and renunciation without yoga does not arise.
sanskrit_cite: yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava | na  hyasaṃnyastasaṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana | evaṃ prāktanenādhyāyagaṇena sādhito'rthaḥ ślokadvayena  nigadyate kāryaṃ-svajātyādivihitam | saṃnyāsī iti yogī iti ca  paryāyāvetau | ata evāha yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti | tathā  ca-yogamantareṇa saṃnyāso nopapadyate evaṃ saṃkalpasaṃnyāsaṃ  vinā yogo na yujyate | tasmātsatatasaṃbaddhau yogasaṃnyāsau | na  niragrirityādināyamartho dhvanyate-niragniśca na bhavati  niṣkriyaśca na bhavati atha ca saṃnyāsī-ityadbhutam

plain_english: Even so, for the sage ascending to yoga action is called the cause, while for the one established in yoga calm itself is called the cause.
sanskrit_cite: tadyapi dyūtamasiṃhāsanaṃ rājyam iti yuktyā ca kevalasya  niṣkriyasya saṃnyāsitvamupapadyate ityuktam tathāpi   ārurukṣormuneryogaṃ karma kāraṇamucyate | yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva  śamaḥ kāraṇamucyate | muneḥ-jñānavataḥ karma-karaṇīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ-prāpakaḥ | śamaḥ-prāptabhūmāvanuparamaḥ | kāraṇamatra lakṣaṇam | eṣa evārthaḥ prakāśyate-

plain_english: When one does not cling to sense objects or actions, that renouncer of all resolves is called established in yoga.
sanskrit_cite: yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasvanuṣajjati | sarvasaṅkalpasaṃnyāsī yogārūḍhastadocyate | indriyārthāḥ-viṣayāḥ | tadarthāni ca  karmāṇi-viṣayārjanādīni | asyāṃ ca buddhāvavaśyamevāvadheyamityāha-

plain_english: One should lift oneself by oneself and not degrade oneself; the self is indeed friend and enemy of itself.
sanskrit_cite: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano  bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ | atra ca nānya upāya apitu ātmaiva-mana evetyarthaḥ

plain_english: For one who has conquered the self by the self, the self is friend; for the unconquered, the self remains like an enemy.
sanskrit_cite: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | ajitātmanastu  śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat | jitaṃ hi mano mitraṃ ghoratarasaṃsāroddharaṇaṃ karoti | ajitaṃ tu  tīvranirayapātanācchatrutvaṃ kurute | tatra jitamanasa idaṃ rūpam-

plain_english: For one who has conquered the self, the tranquil — toward higher and lower selves there is same-mindedness; in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, likewise in honor and dishonor; tranquil, free of ego, with nondual mind unnegated, without attraction and aversion.
sanskrit_cite: jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya parātmasu samāmatiḥ | śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāvamānayoḥ | praśāntaḥ-nirahaṃkāraḥ | pareṣvātmani ca śītoṣṇādiṣu ca  abhedadhīḥ-na rāgadveṣau

plain_english: A yogi is one whose self is satisfied by knowledge and realization, firm-standing, sense-conquered, yoked, and equal to clod, stone, and gold; unerring knowledge is intellect, and where there is various knowledge, that realization is the action previously spoken.
sanskrit_cite: jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ | yukta ityucyate  yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ | jñānam-abhrāntā buddhiḥ | vividhaṃ jñānaṃ yatra  tadvijñānaṃ-prāgyuktyuditaṃ karma

plain_english: Equal-mindedness excels among friends, allies, enemies, neutrals, mediators, saints, and sinners; one who is thus equal-minded gradually excels and crosses samsara.
sanskrit_cite: suhṛnmitrāryudāsīnamadhyasthadveṣyabandhuṣu | sādhuṣvapi ca  pāpeṣu samabuddhirviśiṣyate | suhṛt-yasyākāraṇameva śobhanaṃ hṛdayam | mitratvam anyonyam | aritvaṃ-parasparam | udāsīnaḥ-etadubhayarahitaḥ | madhyasthaḥ-kenacidaṃśena mitraṃ kenacicchattruḥ | dveṣārho  dveṣṭumaśakyo dveṣyaḥ | bandhuḥ-yonyādisaṃbandhena | eteṣu  sarveṣu samadhīḥ | evaṃ sādhuṣu pāpeṣu ca | sa ca  viśiṣyate-kramātkramaṃ saṃsārāttaratti | īdṛśaiśca bandyacaraṇaiḥ-

plain_english: Here creation is conquered by those whose mind is established in equality; Brahman is faultless and equal, so they are established in Brahman. Even while connected to the body, creation is conquered through equality, and for them samsara is non-binding, since they are established in equality, and equality itself is Brahman.
sanskrit_cite: ihaiva tairjitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ | nirdoṣaṃ hi  samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitā | ihaiva-satyapi śarīrasaṃbandhe sargo jitaḥ-sāmyāvasthatvāt | saṃsārasya hyabandhakatvameṣām | sāmye hi te pratiṣṭhitāḥ | sāmyaṃ ca brahma

plain_english: The verse teaches that a yogi seeking ascent should constantly practice in solitude, controlling mind and self, remaining desireless and unpossessive, and making mind and self one-pointed; this is to be done under the proper conditions, not for a limited time.
sanskrit_cite: nanu jitātmanaḥ-ityuktaṃ tatkathaṃ tajjayaḥ ? ityāśaṅkya  ārurukṣoḥ kaścidupāyaḥ kāyasamatvādikaścittasaṃyama  upadiśyate   yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ | ekākī  yatacittātmā nirāśīraparigrahaḥ | ātmānaṃ cittaṃ ca yujjīta-ekāgrīkuryāt | satatamiti-na  parimitaṃ kālam | ekākitvādiṣu satsu etadyujyate nānyathā

plain_english: Having established a firm seat for oneself in a pure place—not too high and not too low—with cloth, deer skin, and kuśa grass on top.
sanskrit_cite: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ | nātyucchritaṃ  nātinīcaṃ cailājinakuśottaram

plain_english: Making the mind one-pointed there, with restrained mind, senses, and actions, sitting on a seat, one should practice yoga for self-purification; by steadiness of seat and time, mind-steadiness arises, and mind-actions and other sense-actions are led into restraint.
sanskrit_cite: tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ | upaviśyāsane  yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye | āsanasthairyātkālasthairye cittasthairyam | cittakriyāḥ-saṃkalpātmānaḥ anyāścendriyakriyā yena  yatāḥ-niyamaṃ nītāḥ

plain_english: Holding body, head, and neck even and motionless, steady, looking at the tip of one's own nose, and not looking at the directions.
sanskrit_cite: samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayannacalaṃ sthiraḥ | saṃpaśyannāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan

plain_english: With calm self, fearless in the celibacy vow, established, having restrained the mind, mind fixed on me, joined, one should sit, devoted to me; holding with effort in looking at the nose tip, not looking at directions, with mind fixed on me, joined, one should sit, thus the meaning.
sanskrit_cite: praśāntātmā vigatabhīrbrahmacārivrate sthitaḥ | manaḥ saṃyamya  maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ | dhārayan-yatnena | nāsāgrasyāvalokane diśāmanavalokanam | matparamatayā yukta āsītetyarthaḥ

plain_english: Thus uniting the self, my devotee with undivided mind attains supreme liberation and my abode; for one who so unites the self, peace arises, in which the final limit of abode is found, and my attainment-yoga exists.
sanskrit_cite: yuñjannevaṃ sadātmānaṃ madbhakto'nanyamānasaḥ | śāntiṃ  nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthāmadhigacchati | evamātmānaṃ yuñjataḥ-samādadhataḥ śāntirjāyate | yasyāṃ  saṃsthāparyantakāṣṭhā matprāptiyogo'stīti

plain_english: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who fasts one-sidedly, nor for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who stays awake too much, Arjuna.
sanskrit_cite: yogo'sti naivātyaśato na caikāntamanaśnataḥ | na  cātisvapnaśīlasya nātijāgarato'rjuna

plain_english: For one moderate in food and recreation, moderate in effort in actions, and moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes pain-removing.
sanskrit_cite: yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu | yuktasvapnāvabodhasya  yogo bhavati duḥkhahā | āhāreṣu-āhiyamāṇeṣu viṣayeṣu | vihāraḥ-upabhogāya  pravṛttiḥ | tasyāśca yuktatvaṃ-nātyantāsaktiḥ  nātyantaparivarjanam | evaṃ sarvatra | śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam | jāgarataḥ- ityādi muneḥ pramāṇatvādredavat | evamanyatrāpi

plain_english: When the restrained mind abides in the self alone, desireless toward all desires, the yogi is called yoked.
sanskrit_cite: yadā viniyataṃ cittamātmanyevāvatiṣṭhate | niḥspṛhaḥ  sarvakāmebhyo yukta ityucyate tadā | asya ca yoginaścihnam ātmanyeva niyatamanāḥ na kiñcidapi spṛhayate

plain_english: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so the yogi's controlled mind does not move; objects and efforts are its movement.
sanskrit_cite: yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā | yogino yatacittasya  yuñjato yogamātmani | yathā nivātastho dīpo na calati evaṃ yogī | calanamasya  viṣayādīnāmarjanādayaḥ prayāsāḥ | idānīṃ tasya svasvabhāvasya brahmaṇo bahutaraviśeṣaṇadvāreṇa  svarūpaṃ nirūpyate tīrthāntarakalpitebhyaśca rūpebhyo  vyatirekaḥ-

plain_english: Where the mind ceases through yoga practice, and the self sees itself in the self, there it is satisfied.
sanskrit_cite: yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yogasevanāt | yatra  caivātmanātmānaṃ paśyannātmani tuṣyati

plain_english: That supreme bliss, beyond the senses and grasped by intellect, is known where one, standing, does not move in truth.
sanskrit_cite: sukhamātyantikaṃ yattad buddhigrāhyamatīndriyam | vetti yatra na  caivāyaṃ sthitaścalati tattvataḥ

plain_english: Having obtained it, one considers no other gain greater; standing in it, one is not shaken even by heavy suffering.
sanskrit_cite: yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ | yasmin  sthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate

plain_english: Know that as yoga, separation from union with suffering; it must be practiced with certainty by an unwearied mind.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ vidyādduḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ yogasaṃjñitam | sa niścayena  yoktavyo yogo'nirviṇnacetasā | yatra mano niruddhamuparamate svayameva  ātyantikaṃ-viṣayakṛtakāluṣyā-bhāvāt sukhaṃ yatra vetti | aparo  lābho-dhanadāraputrādīnām | sanniyogalabdhaśca yogaḥ | anyatra  sukhadhīrnivartate ceti vastusvabhāvo'yamityarthaḥ | na  vicālyate-viśeṣeṇa na cālyate api tu saṃskāramātreṇaivāsya  prathamakṣaṇamātrameva calanaṃ karuṇādivaśāt natu mūḍhatayā  vinaṣṭo vatāhaṃ kiṃ mayā pratipattavyam | ityādi | duḥkhasaṃyogasya viyogo yataḥ | sa ca niścayena-āstikatājanitayā  śraddhayā sarvathā yoktavyaḥ-abhyasanīyaḥ | anirviṇam-upeyaprāptau dṛḍhataraṃ saṃsāraṃ duḥkhabahulaṃ prati  nirviṇaṃ vā ceto yasya | kāmānāṃ tyāge upāyaḥ saṅkalpatyāga ityāha-

plain_english: Abandoning all desires born of resolve, one restrains the whole sense-group by mind on every side.
sanskrit_cite: saṅkalpaprabhavān kāmāṃstyaktvā sarvānaśeṣataḥ | manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ

plain_english: Slowly withdraw by intellect held in firmness, making the mind self-abiding; think nothing at all, thinning desire-sorrow gradually, and do not accept mere object-cessation as the goal.
sanskrit_cite: śanaiḥ śanairuparamedbuddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā | ātmasaṃsthaṃ  manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet | manasaiva-na vyāpāroparameṇa | dhṛtiṃ gṛhītvā  kramātkramamabhilāṣaduḥkhaṃ pratanūkṛtya | kiṃcidapi-viṣayāṇāṃ tyāgagrahaṇādikaṃ na cintayet | yattvanyairvyākhyātaṃ na kiṃcidapi cintayet-iti tadasmabhyaṃ na  rucitaṃ-śūnyavādaprasaṅgāt | na ca viṣayavyuparamamātrameva prāpyamityucyate-

plain_english: Wherever the unsteady mind goes out, restrain it and lead it to calm in the self; otherwise the unstable mind again clings to objects.
sanskrit_cite: yato yato niścarati manaścañcalamasthiram | tatastato  niyamyaitadātmanyeva śamaṃ nayet | yato yato mano nivartate tannivartanasamanantarameva ātmani śamayet | anyathā apratiṣṭhaṃ cittaṃ punarapi viṣayānevāvalambate

plain_english: Supreme happiness approaches the calm-minded yogi who has become brahman and stainless.
sanskrit_cite: praśāntamanasaṃ hyenaṃ yoginaṃ sukhamuttamam | upaiti  śāntarajasaṃ brahmabhūtamakalmaṣam | tatrātmani śāntacittaṃ yoginaṃ-karmabhūtaṃ sukhaṃ  kartṛbhūtamupaiti

plain_english: Thus uniting the self, the yogi with controlled mind attains ultimate union with brahman with ease.
sanskrit_cite: yuñjannevaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ | sukhena  brahmasaṃyogamatyantamadhigacchati | anenaiva krameṇa yogināṃ sukhena brahmāvāptiḥ natu  kaṣṭayogādineti tātparyam

plain_english: The yoga-united self sees the self abiding in all beings and all beings in the self; contemplating the self entering as knower unifies all beings, so equal seeing arises.
sanskrit_cite: sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani | īkṣate  yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ | sarveṣu bhūteṣu ātmānaṃ-grāhakarūpatayānupraviśantaṃ  bhāvayet | ātmani ca grāhyatājñānadvāreṇa sarvāṇi bhūtāni  ekīkuryāt | ataśca samadarśanatvaṃ jāyate yogaśceti  saṃkṣepārthaḥ | vistarastu bhedavādavidāraṇādiprakaraṇe  devīstotravivaraṇe na mayaiva nirṇītaḥ iti tata evāvadhāryaḥ

plain_english: Whoever sees me everywhere and sees all things in me is not lost to me, nor am I lost to him. Destruction comes from non-action. The all-pervading form of the supreme self flees from one who does not see it, since its own form is not manifested. All things are established in the supreme self, the self-illuminator. One who does not see this is lost from true nature, apart from true shining. But one who sees me all-pervading is not lost to me by my own form, through shining; and fears seen in me fit that shining when seership is complete, so such a one is not lost of the supreme self.
sanskrit_cite: yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati | tasyāhaṃ na  praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati | praṇāśaḥ-akāryakāritvāt | tathāhi | paramātmanaḥ sarvagataṃ  rūpaṃ yo na paśyati tasya paramātmā  palāyitaḥ-svarūpaprakaṭīkārābhāvāt | yaccedaṃ vastujātaṃ  tadbhāsanātmani paramātmani viniviṣṭaṃ bhavati tathāvidhaṃ yo na  paśyati sa paramārthasvarūpāt pranaṣṭaḥ-tadvyatireke  satyanirbhāsāt | yastu sarvagataṃ māṃ paśyati tasyāhaṃ na  pranaṣṭaḥ-svasvarūpeṇa bhāsanāt | bhāyāṃśca mayi paśyati  tatteṣāṃ bhāsanopapatto draṣṭṛtāyāṃ paripūrṇāyāṃ sa na  pranaṣṭaḥ paramātmanaḥ

plain_english: He who, established in unity, worships me as present in all beings abides in me though acting in every way; and he who is filled with knowledge, knowing the all-pervading Lord through oneness, is not tainted though he has passed through all states.
sanskrit_cite: sarvabhūtasthitaṃ yo māṃ bhajatyekatvamāsthitaḥ | sarvathā  vartamāno'pi sa yogī mayi vartate | yastvevaṃ jñānāviṣṭaḥ so'vaśyamevaikatayā bhagavantaṃ  sarvagataṃ vidan sarvāvasthāgato'pi na lipyate

plain_english: He who sees everywhere equally by self-likeness, Arjuna, whether pleasure or pain, is considered the supreme yogi; and he sees the pleasure and pain of all as equal to himself. Thus this nature is declared; it is not again a new rule.
sanskrit_cite: ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṃ paśyati yo'rjuna | sukhaṃ vā yadi vā  duḥkhaṃ sa yogī paramo mataḥ | sarvasya ca sukhaduḥkhe ātmatulyatayā paśyati iti  svarūpametadanūditam na punareṣo'pūrvo vidhiḥ

plain_english: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, this yoga of equanimity that you have declared, I do not see its firm stability because of fickleness.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   yo'yaṃ yogastvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana | etasyāhaṃ na  paśyāmi cañcalatvāt sthitiṃ sthirām

plain_english: O Krishna, the mind is unsteady, agitating, strong, and firm; I consider restraining it very difficult, like the wind. Though Brahman is indicated, even clearly and directly, by the sequence of means declared by the Lord through indirect and direct indicators, it remains far away because of the mind's unsteadiness and badness; thus made indirect, it agitates, powerful in seen and unseen matters, and cannot be restrained from firm evil activity. Here is the answer.
sanskrit_cite: cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham | tasyā'haṃ  nigrahaṃ manye vāyoriva suduṣkaram | yo'yamiti-parokṣapratyakṣavācakābhyāmevaṃ sūcyate | bhagavadabhihitānantaropāyaparamparayā  sphuṭamapi-pratyakṣanirdiṣṭamapi brahma  manasaścāñcalyadaurātmyātsudūre vartate iti parokṣāyamāṇam | pramathnāti dṛṣṭādṛṣṭe | balavat-śaktam | dṛḍhaṃ-duṣṭavyāpārāt vārayitumaśakyam | atrottaraṃ-

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: Without doubt, O mighty-armed one, the mind is hard to restrain and restless; yet by practice and by detachment it is grasped. By detachment, eagerness for objects is destroyed; by practice, the side of liberation is progressively made an object. Thus the taking up of both is stated; and there, by you, the commentator says restraint of mind-modifications depends on both—though the final token remains unclear.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṃ calam | abhyāsena tu kaunteya  vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate | varāgyeṇa viṣayotsukatā vināśyate | abhyāsena mokṣapakṣaḥ  kramātkramaṃ viṣayīkriyate iti dvayorupādānam | uktaṃ ca tatra  bhavatā bhāṣyakṛtā   ubhayādhīnaścittavṛttinirodhaḥ | (yo0 da0 1, 12)   iti

plain_english: Yoga is hard for an uncontrolled self, but attainable by a controlled, striving self through practice and prescribed means.
sanskrit_cite: asaṃyatātmano yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ | vaśyātmanā tu yatatā  śakyo'vāptumupāyataḥ | ata eṣā pratijñā-asaṃyatātmanaḥ-aviraktasya na  kathaṃcidyogāvāptiḥ | vaśyātmaneti-vairāgyavatā | yatamāneneti-sābhyāsena | upāyān-anekasiddhāntādiśāstravihitān  saṃśritya

plain_english: Arjuna asks about one endowed with faith whose mind has deviated from yoga and who is confused on the path of brahman.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   ayataḥ śraddhayopeto yogāccalitamānasaḥ | lipsamānaḥ satāṃ  mārgaṃ pramūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi

plain_english: Arjuna asks what course one takes who, confused and deluded, fails to attain yoga perfection, noting that faith may remain even if the mind deviates.
sanskrit_cite: anekacittovibhrānto mohasyaiva vaśaṃ gataḥ | aprāpya  yogasaṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati | prāptādyogāt yadi calite'pi citte śraddhā na hīyate vinaṣṭa  śraddho hi siddhayogo'pi sarvaṃ niṣphalaṃ kurute | uktaṃ hi   yadā prāpyāpi vijñānaṃ dūṣitaṃ cittavibhramāt | tadaiva  dhvaṃsate śrīghraṃ tūlarāśirivānalāt iti

plain_english: Arjuna asks whether one who loses both yoga and brahman perishes like a cut cloud or attains destruction.
sanskrit_cite: kaccinnobhayavibhraṃśācchinnābhramiva naśyati | apratiṣṭho  mahābāho vināśaṃ vādhigacchati

plain_english: Arjuna asks Krishna to cut his doubt completely, since no one else can resolve whether a failed yogi perishes or remains unestablished.
sanskrit_cite: etanme saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇa cchettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ | tvadanyaḥ  saṃśayasyāsya chettā na hyupapadyate | yogasya samyak siddhāvajātāyāṃ kiṃ lokānniṣkrāntaḥ samyak ca  brahmaṇi na līnaḥ iti naśyet athavā  brahmaṇyapratiṣṭhatvādvinaśyati paralokabādhāya iti praśnaḥ | atra nirṇayaṃ-

plain_english: Krishna says there is no destruction for such a person in this world or the next, because a doer of good never goes to a bad course and faith is not lost.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśastasya vidyate | na hi kalyāṇakṛt  kaścid durgatiṃ jātu gacchati | na tasya yogabhraṣṭasyeha loke paraloke vā  nāśo'sti-anaṣṭaśraddhatvāditi bhāvaḥ | tasya-lokadvayāvināśinaḥ | sa hi kalyāṇaṃ  bhagavanmārgalakṣaṇaṃ kṛtavān | na ca tadagniṣṭomādivatkṣayi

plain_english: Having attained and dwelt for eternal years in meritorious worlds, the one fallen from yoga is born in the house of pure and prosperous people; there are three eternal Vaishnava years of eternal Vishnu; this concerns those called pure whose minds touch a portion of the divine.
sanskrit_cite: prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃllokānuṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ | śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo'bhijāyate | śāśvatasya-viṣṇoḥ samāḥ-vaiṣṇavāni trīṇi varṣāṇi | śucīnāmiti-yeṣāṃ bhagavadaṃśasparśi cittam

plain_english: Or, such a birth arises only in the family of wise yogis; indeed this birth is rarer in the world. But if there must be gradation in its release, then it arises indeed in a yogi family. Thus it is said: this is rarer indeed. In the house of the prosperous, surely obstacles necessarily exist in accomplishment of liberation.
sanskrit_cite: athavā yogināmeva jāyate dhīmatāṃ kule | etaddhi durlabhataraṃ  loke janma yadīdṛśam | yadi tu tāratamyenāsyāpavargeṇa bhavitavyaṃ tadā yogikula eva  jāyate | eta evāha-etaddhi durlabhataram-iti | śrīmatāṃ gehe  kilāvaśyameva vighnāḥ santi saṃsiddhau mokṣātmikāyām

plain_english: There he regains the intelligence-connection of his former life; then he strives again for perfection, O son of Kuru.
sanskrit_cite: tatra taṃ buddhisaṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadaihikam | tatobhūyo'pi  yatate saṃsiddhau kurunandana

plain_english: By previous practice one is carried even unwilling; even one desiring to know yoga transcends word-Brahman. Indeed, even unwilling and dependent, by that previous practice alone one is forcibly led to yoga practice. This is not ordinary: mere inquiry into yoga alone does not transcend word-Brahman; word-Brahman in the form of mantra-study and the like is not transcended but taken up.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hyavaśo'pi san | jijñāsurapi  yogasya śabdabrahmātivartate | avaśaḥ-paratantra eva kila tena-pūrvābhyāsena balādeva  yogābhyāsaṃ prati nīyate | na caitat sāmānyaṃ  yogajijñāsāmātreṇaiva hi śabdabrahmātivṛttiḥ  mantrasvādhyāyādirūpaṃ ca śabdabrahma ativartate-na svīkurute

plain_english: A yogi who strives earnestly, is purified of sin, and perfected through many births goes to the supreme goal; after inquiry and diligent practice he attains Vasudeva-state at death, not by that body alone but through many births of practice; one whose sole occupation is devotion to divine activity is to be judged fallen from yoga, declaring yoga's preeminence.
sanskrit_cite: prayatnādyatamānastu yogī saṃśuddhakilviṣaḥ | anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yāti parāṃ gatim | tato-jijñāsānantaram yatnavān-abhyāsakrameṇa dehānte  vāsudevatvaṃ prāpnoti | na cāsau tenaiva dehena siddha iti mantavyam  apitu bahūni janmāni tena tadabhyastamiti mantavyam | ata eva  yasyānanyavyāpāratayā bhagavadvyāpārānurāgitvaṃ sa  yogabhraṣṭa iti niśceyam | yogasya prādhānyamāha-

plain_english: The yogi is greater than ascetics, knowers, and workers; therefore, Arjuna, be a yogi. His superiority to ascetics was already shown; to knowers, because knowledge is yoga's fruit; to workers, because he knows what actions to do, and mere strenuous yoga without the Lord is not said to bring perfection.
sanskrit_cite: tapasvibhyo'dhiko yogī jñānibhyo'pi mato'dhikaḥ | karmibhyaścādhiko yogī tasmād yogī bhavārjuna | tapasvibhyo'dhikatvaṃ pūrvameva sūcitam | jñānibhyo'dhikatvaṃjñānasya yogaphalatvāt | karmibhya  utkarṣaḥ-sa eva karmāṇi kartuṃ vetti | na ca nirīśvaraṃ kaṣṭayogamātraṃ saṃsiddhidamityucyate-

plain_english: Among all yogins, the faithful one who worships the Lord with inner self turned toward Him is considered most united; he places the Lord in the inner organ, is devoted to devotion and faith, and by the tradition-order obtained through service to the guru's feet worships and reflects on the Lord alone, not another; he is most united, entered into the supreme Lord. Thus the supremacy of all knowing with the Lord is declared. Auspicious. 49.
sanskrit_cite: yogināmapi sarveṣāṃ madgatenāntarātmanā | śraddhāvān bhajate  yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ | sarvayogimadhye ya eva māmantaḥkaraṇe niveśya bhaktiśraddhātatparo  gurucaraṇasevālabdhasaṃpradāyakrameṇa māmeva-nānyat  bhajatevimṛśyate sa yuktatamaḥ-parameśvarasamāviṣṭaḥ iti  seśvarasya jñānasya sarvaprādhānyamuktamiti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: all is obtained by mere attainment of the Lord's name, as rice plants ripen when proper rain alone is seen. 6. Thus in the gathering of the meaning of the holy Bhagavad Gita, composed by the feet of Abhinavagupta, the sixth chapter. 6.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   bhagavannāmasaṃprāptimātrātsarvamavāpyate | phalitāḥ śālayaḥ  samyagvṛṣṭimātre'valokite | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ
